title: 扎克伯格如何在裁员信中承认判断失误、承担责任（2022）
topic: 扎克伯格如何在裁员信中承认判断失误、承担责任（2022）

source.title: Mark Zuckerberg’s Message to Meta Employees
source.license: 原文按项目方确认的授权收录
source.context: Mark Zuckerberg 于 2022-11-09 发布的员工信。内容区分裁员规模、疫情期间电商增长预期、后续市场变化、本人承担责任及对受影响员工的歉意；属于当时公告。
paragraphs: Mark Zuckerberg just shared the following with Meta employees:

Today I’m sharing some of the most difficult changes we’ve made in Meta’s history. I’ve decided to reduce the size of our team by about 13% and let more than 11,000 of our talented employees go. We are also taking a number of additional steps to become a leaner and more efficient company by cutting discretionary spending and extending our hiring freeze through Q1.
I want to take accountability for these decisions and for how we got here. I know this is tough for everyone, and I’m especially sorry to those impacted.

At the start of Covid, the world rapidly moved online and the surge of e-commerce led to outsized revenue growth. Many people predicted this would be a permanent acceleration that would continue even after the pandemic ended. I did too, so I made the decision to significantly increase our investments. Unfortunately, this did not play out the way I expected. Not only has online commerce returned to prior trends, but the macroeconomic downturn, increased competition, and ads signal loss have caused our revenue to be much lower than I’d expected. I got this wrong, and I take responsibility for that.
translations: 扎克伯格刚刚向Meta员工分享了以下内容：
今天，我要分享 Meta 历史上一些最艰难的调整。我决定将团队规模缩减约 13%，裁减超过 11,000 名员工。我们还将采取其他措施，让公司运营更精简、高效，包括削减非必要支出，并将招聘冻结延长至第一季度。
我想为这些决定以及我们如何走到这一步承担责任。我知道这对每个人来说都很艰难，对于那些受到影响的人，我尤其感到抱歉。
新冠疫情初期，世界迅速转向线上，电商激增带来了异常强劲的收入增长。许多人认为，这种增长加速会永久持续，疫情结束后也不会停止。我当时也这么判断，因此决定大幅增加投资。遗憾的是，实际情况并非如此：线上商业已回归此前趋势，再加上宏观经济下行、竞争加剧和广告信号损失，收入远低于我的预期。这是我的判断失误，我愿意承担责任。
fullTextParagraphs: Mark Zuckerberg just shared the following with Meta employees:

Today I’m sharing some of the most difficult changes we’ve made in Meta’s history. I’ve decided to reduce the size of our team by about 13% and let more than 11,000 of our talented employees go. We are also taking a number of additional steps to become a leaner and more efficient company by cutting discretionary spending and extending our hiring freeze through Q1.
I want to take accountability for these decisions and for how we got here. I know this is tough for everyone, and I’m especially sorry to those impacted.

At the start of Covid, the world rapidly moved online and the surge of e-commerce led to outsized revenue growth. Many people predicted this would be a permanent acceleration that would continue even after the pandemic ended. I did too, so I made the decision to significantly increase our investments. Unfortunately, this did not play out the way I expected. Not only has online commerce returned to prior trends, but the macroeconomic downturn, increased competition, and ads signal loss have caused our revenue to be much lower than I’d expected. I got this wrong, and I take responsibility for that.

In this new environment, we need to become more capital efficient. We’ve shifted more of our resources onto a smaller number of high priority growth areas — like our AI discovery engine, our ads and business platforms, and our long-term vision for the metaverse. We’ve cut costs across our business, including scaling back budgets, reducing perks, and shrinking our real estate footprint. We’re restructuring teams to increase our efficiency. But these measures alone won’t bring our expenses in line with our revenue growth, so I’ve also made the hard decision to let people go.
There is no good way to do a layoff, but we hope to get all the relevant information to you as quickly as possible and then do whatever we can to support you through this.

Everyone will get an email soon letting you know what this layoff means for you. After that, every affected employee will have the opportunity to speak with someone to get their questions answered and join information sessions.
Some of the details in the US include:
Severance. We will pay 16 weeks of base pay plus two additional weeks for every year of service, with no cap.
PTO. We’ll pay for all remaining PTO time.
RSU vesting. Everyone impacted will receive their November 15, 2022 vesting.
Health insurance. We’ll cover the cost of healthcare for people and their families for six months.
Career services. We’ll provide three months of career support with an external vendor, including early access to unpublished job leads.

Immigration support. I know this is especially difficult if you’re here on a visa. There’s a notice period before termination and some visa grace periods, which means everyone will have time to make plans and work through their immigration status. We have dedicated immigration specialists to help guide you based on what you and your family need.
Outside the US, support will be similar, and we’ll follow up soon with separate processes that take into account local employment laws.

We made the decision to remove access to most Meta systems for people leaving today given the amount of access to sensitive information. But we’re keeping email addresses active throughout the day so everyone can say farewell.

While we’re making reductions in every organization across both Family of Apps and Reality Labs, some teams will be affected more than others. Recruiting will be disproportionately affected since we’re planning to hire fewer people next year. We’re also restructuring our business teams more substantially. This is not a reflection of the great work these groups have done, but what we need going forward. The leaders of each group will schedule time to discuss what this means for your team over the next couple of days.

The teammates who will be leaving us are talented and passionate, and have made an important impact on our company and community. Each of you have helped make Meta a success, and I’m grateful for it. I’m sure you’ll go on to do great work at other places.

I view layoffs as a last resort, so we decided to rein in other sources of cost before letting teammates go. Overall, this will add up to a meaningful cultural shift in how we operate. For example, as we shrink our real estate footprint, we’re transitioning to desk sharing for people who already spend most of their time outside the office. We’ll roll out more cost-cutting changes like this in the coming months.

We’re also extending our hiring freeze through Q1 with a small number of exceptions. I’m going to watch our business performance, operational efficiency, and other macroeconomic factors to determine whether and how much we should resume hiring at that point. This will give us the ability to control our cost structure in the event of a continued economic downturn. It will also put us on a path to achieve a more efficient cost structure than we outlined to investors recently.

I’m currently in the middle of a thorough review of our infrastructure spending. As we build our AI infrastructure, we’re focused on becoming even more efficient with our capacity. Our infrastructure will continue to be an important advantage for Meta, and I believe we can achieve this while spending less.

Fundamentally, we’re making all these changes for two reasons: our revenue outlook is lower than we expected at the beginning of this year, and we want to make sure we’re operating efficiently across both Family of Apps and Reality Labs.

This is a sad moment, and there’s no way around that. To those who are leaving, I want to thank you again for everything you’ve put into this place. We would not be where we are today without your hard work, and I’m grateful for your contributions.

To those who are staying, I know this is a difficult time for you too. Not only are we saying goodbye to people we’ve worked closely with, but many of you also feel uncertainty about the future. I want you to know that we’re making these decisions to make sure our future is strong.

I believe we are deeply underestimated as a company today. Billions of people use our services to connect, and our communities keep growing. Our core business is among the most profitable ever built with huge potential ahead. And we’re leading in developing the technology to define the future of social connection and the next computing platform. We do historically important work. I’m confident that if we work efficiently, we’ll come out of this downturn stronger and more resilient than ever.

We’ll share more on how we’ll operate as a streamlined organization to achieve our priorities in the weeks ahead. For now, I’ll say one more time how thankful I am to those of you who are leaving for everything you’ve done to advance our mission.

This post contains forward-looking statements regarding our future business plans and expectations. These forward-looking statements are only predictions and may differ materially from actual results due to a variety of factors. Because some of these risks and uncertainties cannot be predicted or quantified and some are beyond our control, you should not rely on our forward-looking statements as predictions of future events. More information about potential risks and uncertainties that could affect our business and financial results is more fully detailed under the caption “Risk Factors” in our Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on October 27, 2022, which is available on our Investor Relations website at investor.fb.com and on the SEC website at www.sec.gov. In addition, please note that the date of this post is November 9, 2022, and any forward-looking statements contained herein are based on assumptions that we believe to be reasonable as of this date. fullTextHeadings.18: WHAT OTHER CHANGES ARE WE MAKING?

notes.phrase: Mark Zuckerberg just shared the following with Meta employees:
notes.meaning: 扎克伯格刚刚向 Meta 员工分享了以下内容
notes.explain: 这是引出员工信的开场句；不应误以为它是信件正文中的第一人称叙述。
notes.example: The CEO shared the following update with employees.

notes.phrase: reduce the size of our team by about 13%
notes.explain: about 表示约数；同句还写了超过 11,000 名员工，因此邮件同时给出比例和人数。
notes.example: The proposal would reduce the team by about 8%, or roughly 40 people.

notes.phrase: I want to take accountability for these decisions
notes.meaning: 我想为这些决定承担责任
notes.explain: take accountability for 后接要负责的决定或结果；这里不是把原因归咎于团队。
notes.example: I want to take accountability for the decision and explain what I learned.

notes.phrase: the surge of e-commerce led to outsized revenue growth
notes.meaning: 电商激增带来异常强劲的收入增长
notes.explain: outsized 强调增长规模异常大；后文才说明他预测这一趋势会持续，并承认自己判断错了。
notes.example: The product launch led to outsized growth in subscriptions.

notes.phrase: I got this wrong, and I take responsibility for that.
notes.meaning: 我判断错了，我愿意为此承担责任
notes.explain: 前半句承认判断错误，后半句明确责任归属；that 回指前面的判断和投资决定。
notes.example: I got the forecast wrong, and I take responsibility for that.

scenario.title: Explaining the forecast error and acknowledging its impact
english: A colleague asks what Mark Zuckerberg said about Meta’s 2022 layoffs and how he explained his own role in the decision.

He expected the pandemic-era surge in e-commerce to continue, so he increased investment. It did not play out as he expected; he said online commerce returned to prior trends and cited a downturn, stronger competition, and ads signal loss as additional pressures.
You summarize his forecast, the result, his admission of error, and his apology to affected employees without suggesting that one cause explains everything.
chinese: 一位同事问，Mark Zuckerberg 如何说明 Meta 2022 年的裁员，以及他怎样谈到自己在决策中的责任。
他表示，自己原以为疫情期间电商激增会持续，因此增加了投资。实际情况并非如此；他提到线上商业回归此前趋势，也提到经济下行、竞争加剧和广告信号损失等额外压力。
你概括他的预期、实际结果、认错和对受影响员工的歉意，不把其中某一个原因说成全部原因。

firstAttempt.prompt: 重点读员工信开头关于增长预期和责任的段落。请用两到三句英文概括他原先的预期、实际结果、如何承担责任，以及对受影响员工说了什么。
firstAttempt.sample: He expected the pandemic-era surge in e-commerce to continue, so he increased investment. It did not play out the way he expected; he said, “I got this wrong,” took responsibility, and said he was especially sorry to those impacted.
firstAttempt.rationale: 先概括预测和结果，再说清承认判断失误、承担责任及对员工的回应。

words.example: We reviewed discretionary spending before approving the event budget.
words.translation: 我们在批准活动预算前审查了可自由支配的开支。
words.note: 通常指可以推迟、削减或由组织决定是否支出的费用。

words.example: The e-commerce surge led to outsized revenue growth.
words.translation: 电商激增带来了异常强劲的收入增长。
words.note: outsized 表示规模明显偏大；本身不等于“超过预测”。

words.example: The memo cited a macroeconomic downturn as one pressure on revenue.
words.translation: 备忘录把宏观经济下行列为收入受到压力的一个原因。
words.note: 宏观经济层面的放缓；不要和某家公司内部经营问题混为一谈。

words.example: The CEO cited ads signal loss as one of several pressures on revenue.
words.translation: CEO 将广告信号损失列为收入承压的因素之一。
words.note: 这是原信中的行业术语；信中没有说它是收入下降的唯一原因。

words.example: The message described the employees leaving as talented and passionate colleagues.
words.translation: 信中称离开的员工是有才干、充满热情的同事。
words.note: talented 描述能力；不要据此推断岗位调整只涉及某一绩效层级。

words.example: Meta extended its hiring freeze through Q1, with a small number of exceptions.
words.translation: Meta 将招聘冻结延长至第一季度，只有少数例外。
words.note: 这是该封 2022 年邮件宣布的安排，不代表现行政策。

structure.original: I got this wrong, and I take responsibility for that.
analysis: I got this wrong 是一般过去时，说明说话人现在回看过去的预测并承认判断有误。
and 连接两个完整分句；第二句用现在时 take responsibility 表示现在仍承担责任。
for that 中的 that 指前文的判断或决定；take responsibility for 后接名词或动名词。
structure.transfer: I got the rollout forecast wrong, and I take responsibility for that.

rewrite.bad: The market changed. The forecast missed, so let’s move on.
rewrite.good: I expected the pandemic-era surge in e-commerce to continue, so I increased investment. That did not play out as I expected. I got this wrong, and I take responsibility for that. I’m especially sorry to those impacted.
rewrite.translation: 我原以为疫情期间的电商激增会持续，因此增加了投资。实际情况并非如此。我判断错了，我愿意为此承担责任。我尤其对受到影响的人感到抱歉。
rewrite.pattern: I expected [trend] to continue, so I [decision]. It did not happen as expected. I got this wrong, and I take responsibility. I’m sorry to [people impacted].

cloze.prompt: Many people thought the e-commerce surge would be a permanent ___.
cloze.why: acceleration 指增长或变化速度加快；Zuckerberg 说自己也作了同样预测。

cloze.prompt: I got this wrong, and I take ___ for that.
cloze.why: take responsibility for 表示为判断或决定承担责任。
those impacted 指受到影响的人；原信用的是 impacted。

dictation.text: I want to take accountability for these decisions and for how we got here.
dictation.label: 听写 1 · 承担决策责任
dictation.why: 这是员工信原句，直接说明责任归属。

dictation.text: I got this wrong, and I take responsibility for that.
dictation.label: 听写 2 · 承认预测失误
dictation.why: 这是员工信原句，注意过去判断和当前承担责任的时态变化。

apply.prompt: 一位同事说，预测没实现完全是市场的问题。用一句英文说明负责人如何承担责任。
apply.sample: I got this wrong, and I take responsibility for that decision.

translationPractice.prompt: 我原以为电商激增会持续，但实际并非如此。
translationPractice.answer: I expected the e-commerce surge to continue, but it did not.
translationPractice.why: 说明原先的预期与后来的结果不同，不添加新的市场原因。

translationPractice.prompt: 我判断错了，我愿意为此承担责任。
translationPractice.answer: I got this wrong, and I take responsibility for that.
translationPractice.why: 保留原信中承认判断失误并承担责任的两个动作。

translationPractice.prompt: 我尤其对受到影响的人感到抱歉。
translationPractice.answer: I’m especially sorry to those impacted.
translationPractice.why: 与原信中的道歉对象一致，不擅自增加具体个人或团队。

choice.prompt: 哪一项准确概括 Zuckerberg 对自己预测失误的解释？
options: He expected the pandemic-era e-commerce surge to continue, increased investment, and later said the trend returned to prior levels while other pressures also reduced revenue.
He expected e-commerce to return to prior trends, so he reduced investment before the pandemic ended.
He said the layoffs were caused only by employee performance and that he had no responsibility for the forecast.
choice.why: 他说明自己预期电商加速会持续并因此加大投资，随后承认实际情况不同；信中还列出经济下行、竞争和广告信号损失等压力。

output.prompt: （模拟情景）团队原以为新客服工具能缩短回复时间，但试点没有改善。请用英文向团队说明预期与结果，承认判断失误并承担责任，再向受影响的人道歉。
output.sample: I expected the new support tool to reduce response times, but it did not. I got this wrong, and I take responsibility for that decision. I’m sorry to the teams affected by the change.
check: 是否说明原先预期和实际结果？
是否承认判断失误并承担责任？
是否向受影响的人表达歉意？
是否没有把 Meta 的人数或市场原因移植到模拟情景？

credits.audio: 美式英语合成朗读，非公司员工原声。
credits.illustration: 通用团队沟通场景示意图；非 Meta 员工、管理者或真实邮件场景。
